hints.title: User Annual Purchase Volume Aggregation
hints.text: Report each user join date and total orders placed as a buyer throughout calendar year 2019, including zero counts.

hints.title: Left Join with Filter Predicate in Join Condition
hints.text: Left join users to orders matching buyer identifier and 2019 order dates, grouping by user identifier to count orders.

hints.title: Market Analysis Query Blueprint
hints.text: select u.user_id as buyer_id, u.join_date, count(o.order_id) as orders_in_2019 from Users u left join Orders o on u.user_id = o.buyer_id and o.order_date between "2019-01-01" and "2019-12-31" group by u.user_id, u.join_date.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT u.user_id AS buyer_id, u.join_date,
       COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_in_2019
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON u.user_id = o.buyer_id AND o.order_date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-31'
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.join_date;
```

complexity.notes: Left join followed by grouping on user identifier runs in linear time relative to table sizes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Filtering orders in a where clause turns the left join into an inner join, discarding users with zero purchases.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Condition placed inside ON clause preserves all users while filtering order rows.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Placing the date condition in the ON clause of the LEFT JOIN to retain users with 0 orders.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def market_analysis(users: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame, items: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    orders_2019 = orders[(orders['order_date'] >= '2019-01-01') & (orders['order_date'] <= '2019-12-31')]
    counts = orders_2019.groupby('buyer_id')['order_id'].count().reset_index()
    counts = counts.rename(columns={'order_id': 'orders_in_2019'})
    merged = users.merge(counts, left_on='user_id', right_on='buyer_id', how='left')
    merged['orders_in_2019'] = merged['orders_in_2019'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    merged = merged.rename(columns={'user_id': 'buyer_id'})
    return merged[['buyer_id', 'join_date', 'orders_in_2019']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Left Merge with Zero Fill
